rows.jyutping: mong4 jan1 fu6 ji6 ge3 jan4
rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when you mean someone who fails to appreciate help or kindness received.

example.english: They’re such an ingrate—they called me meddlesome after I helped them.
example.traditional: 佢真係個忘恩負義嘅人，幫完佢仲話我多事。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 go3 mong4 jan1 fu6 ji6 ge3 jan4 bong1 jyun4 keoi5 zung6 waa6 ngo5 do1 si6

rows.note: Use this casual insult for the unpleasant or contemptible-person side of “ingrate,” especially in an outburst.

example.english: You ingrate, I helped you and you still complained about everything!
example.jyutping: seoi1 jan4 bong1 nei5 zung6 jim4 saam1 jim4 sei3

rows.note: Use this when stressing that someone repays kindness with ingratitude; it is less common in everyday Hong Kong speech than the other choices.

example.english: I once saved them, but they betrayed me right afterward—they’re a real ingrate.
example.traditional: 我救過佢一次，點知佢轉頭就出賣我，真係白眼狼。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gau3 gwo3 keoi5 jat1 ci3 dim2 zi1 keoi5 zyun3 tau4 zau6 ceot1 maai6 ngo5 zan1 hai6 baak6 ngaan5 long4
